How a job runs

  1. 1

    Post it or call it

    Boat, engine, what it's doing and where it sits. Two minutes.

  2. 2

    We call back and dispatch

    A dispatcher confirms the details, then offers the job to the two or three insured mechanics nearest you who work on your engine.

  3. 3

    A mechanic comes to the boat

    The first to accept texts you their name and a time. You approve a written quote before any work starts.

  4. 4

    Pay when it's done

    You get an itemized invoice by text or email. Pay by bank with no fee, or by card.

Engines we work on

Jobs are matched by brand, so a Yamaha owner gets a mechanic who carries Yamaha service kits and reads Yamaha fault codes.

  • YamahaF25 through F450, F150 and F200 four-strokes, VMAX SHO, older HPDI and OX66 two-strokes
  • MercuryFourStroke 40 to 150, Pro XS, Verado 200 to 400, SeaPro, older OptiMax and two-strokes
  • SuzukiDF25 through DF350A, including the DF140A, DF200 and DF300 family
  • Honda MarineBF2.3 through BF250, with the BF90, BF150 and BF225 common locally
  • TohatsuMFS 2.5 through MFS 140, and Nissan-branded twins
  • Evinrude and JohnsonE-TEC G1 and G2, older Ficht and carbureted two-strokes, Johnson
  • MerCruiserAlpha One and Bravo drives, 3.0 through 8.2 gas inboards, MPI and carbureted
  • Volvo PentaSX and DPS gas drives, D3 through D6 diesels, IPS pods on larger yachts
  • Yanmar1GM through 4JH sailboat diesels, 6LY and 8LV cruiser diesels

Why not just call a shop?

Shops are weeks out in season

Mobile mechanics usually see you within a few days, often the same day for a boat that won't start.

No trailering, no yard fees

The work happens on your lift or in your slip. You don't need to be there.

Still a real mechanic

Independent and insured, matched to your engine, with a written quote and reviews from every job.

Questions we get

Is posting a job really free?

Yes. You pay the mechanic for the work, through a payment link, after it is done. There is no fee to post or to get a quote.

Who are the mechanics?

Independent marine mechanics and small shops in Tampa Bay, checked for experience and insurance, who have signed our standards agreement. Each job goes to mechanics who work on your engine brand near your zip code.

How fast can someone come?

Routine service is usually scheduled within a few days. A boat that won't start at the ramp or on a lift can often be seen the same day; call rather than post for those.

How do I pay?

When the work is done you get a link. Pay by bank transfer with no fee, or by card with a small processing fee shown up front. We pay the mechanic.

Boat won't start at the ramp? Call, and the nearest mechanic heads over.
